Let H ⊂ GL(2, ℤ/n).

Corollary 2.2. The fiber product

Spec(ℤ[[q]]) ×_{𝓜₁} 𝓜_H

is the spectrum of the normalization of ℤ[[q]] in the affine algebra of the finite étale scheme over ℤ[[q]][1/n, 1/q]

Isom((𝔾_m^q/q^ℤ)_n, (ℤ/n)²)/H.

Proof. This follows from the definitions and from the fact that normalization and completion commute.

Since the group scheme (𝔾_m^q/q^ℤ)_n over ℤ[[q]][1/q] was computed in 1.15, 2.2 makes it possible to describe explicitly the structure of 𝓜_H at infinity.

2.3. We shall treat the case of 𝓜_n (n ≥ 3), considered as an algebraic stack over ℤ[ζ_n]. If the supersingular points of characteristic p | n are removed from 𝓜_n, the resulting stack 𝓜_n^h is a scheme, described in modular terms in V 4.

Let C be the standard Néron n-gon over ℤ[ζ_n], endowed with its structure of generalized elliptic curve (1.9) and with the natural isomorphism

C_n = μ_n × ℤ/n.

This curve defines a section at infinity

(2.3.1)  f_n : Spec(ℤ[ζ_n]) → 𝓜_n.

Corollary 2.4. The morphism (2.3.2) identifies ℤ[ζ_n][[q^{1/n}]] with the formal completion of 𝓜_n along the section at infinity f_n.

Proof. This can be deduced from 2.2. It is simpler to repeat the proof of 2.1, using the facts that

(a) 𝓜_n is smooth over ℤ[ζ_n] in a neighborhood of infinity;

(b) the image on Spec(ℤ[ζ_n][[q^{1/n}]]) of the nonsmooth locus of 𝔾_m^{q^{1/n}} is defined by the equation q^{1/n} = 0.

±U = { ±( 1  * ; 0  1 ) }.

Corollary 2.5. If n ≥ 3, the completion of 𝓜_n^h along infinity is a sum of copies of Spec(ℤ[ζ_n][[q^{1/n}]]), indexed by SL(2, ℤ/n)/±U.

Corollary 2.6. Let C be a generalized elliptic curve over a complete local ring A. Suppose that C is not smooth; let (t) be the ideal of A that defines the nonsmoothness subscheme. Suppose that the special fiber C_s of C has k sides and that Gal(s̄/s) acts trivially on the diagram Γ(C_s̄) of the irreducible components of C_s̄. Then there exists u ∈ A* such that

C ≅ 𝔾_m^t/(ut^k)^ℤ.

Proof. Let X_v be the group scheme over ℤ[v, v^{-1}], an extension of ℤ/k by μ_k,

0 → μ_k → X_v →^{φ} ℤ/k → 0,

such that φ^{-1}(1) is the μ_k-torsor of kth roots of v. Let 𝒢_v be the algebraic stack over ℤ[v, v^{-1}] classifying generalized elliptic curves E over a ℤ[v, v^{-1}]-scheme, smooth or k-sided, endowed with an isomorphism E_k ≅ X_v. After scalar extension to ℤ[v^{1/k}], X_v becomes isomorphic to μ_k × ℤ/k, and 𝒢_v to 𝒢 of V 4.4. The map

Spec(ℤ[v, v^{-1}][[τ]]) → 𝒢_v

defined by the curve 𝔾_m^τ/(vτ^k)^ℤ therefore identifies Spec(ℤ[v, v^{-1}][[τ]]) with the formal completion of 𝒢_v along a section at infinity.

Under the hypotheses of 2.6, there exists v ∈ A* such that C_k is isomorphic to X_v and C_s to 𝔾_m^τ/(vτ^k)^ℤ over k(s). The curve C is therefore the pullback of the curve 𝔾_m^τ/(vτ^k)^ℤ over ℤ[v, v^{-1}][[τ]], and 2.6 follows.

3. Application: expansion of a modular form as a Fourier series.

We shall show in § 4 that, after scalar extension to ℂ, the notions introduced in this section coincide with the classical notions.

Definition 3.1. The algebra of integral modular forms is the graded algebra

⊕_k H⁰(𝓜₁, ω^{⊗k}).

In other words, an integral modular form of weight k is a rule, compatible with base change, which to C/S, an irreducible generalized elliptic curve over a scheme S, associates a section of ω^{⊗k} over S.

Definition 3.2. The algebra of integral modular forms of level H ⊂ GL(2, ℤ/n) is the graded algebra

⊕_k H⁰(𝓜_H, ω^{⊗k}).

The following lemma makes it possible, in certain cases, to consider only the 𝓜_n.

Lemma 3.3. We have

H⁰(𝓜_H, ω^{⊗k}) ≃ H⁰(𝓜_n, ω^{⊗k})^H.

Proof. Since 𝓜_H^∘[1/n] ≃ [𝓜_n^∘[1/n]/H] (notation as in [8], § 4), we have

H⁰(𝓜_H^∘[1/n], ω^{⊗k}) ≃ H⁰(𝓜_n^∘[1/n], ω^{⊗k})^H.

We conclude by the normality of 𝓜_H: for a rational section of ω^{⊗k} on 𝓜_H to be defined everywhere, it is enough that its pullback to the finite covering

Theorem 3.4. The algebra of integral modular forms of level H is a finitely generated ℤ-algebra.

Proof. By 3.3, it is enough to treat the case of 𝓜_n, for n large. In this case 𝓜_n = M_n is a projective scheme over ℤ, and ω is an ample invertible sheaf on M_n. Indeed, the divisor of the section Δ of ω^{⊗12} is a multiple of M_n^∞ (on 𝓜_n, div(Δ) = 𝓜_n^∞); it meets every irreducible component of every fiber of M_n over ℤ, and is therefore ample. The theorem consequently follows from the general theorem EGA III, 2.3.4.1.

3.5. One may also consider modular forms with coefficients in algebras over ℤ. Since we are not sure of the correct definition in the general case, we shall for the most part restrict ourselves to the case of the 𝓜_n, viewed as ℤ[ζ_n]-stacks.

Definition 3.6. Let A be an algebra over ℤ[ζ_n]. A modular form of level n and weight k over the ℤ[ζ_n]-algebra A is an element of

H⁰(𝓜_n ⊗_{ℤ[ζ_n]} A, ω^{⊗k}).

3.7. Let φ be a modular form (cf. 3.6). Evaluate φ on the n-sided Tate curve 𝔾_m^{q^{1/n}}/q^ℤ over A[[q^{1/n}]]: the Tate curve defines a morphism (2.1)

τ : Spec(A[[q^{1/n}]]) → 𝓜_n ⊗_{ℤ[ζ_n]} A;

the pullback of ω by τ is trivialized (by the section dx/x (1.12)); hence

τ*φ = f_φ(q)(dx/x)^{⊗k},  with f_φ(q) ∈ A[[q^{1/n}]].

We call f_φ the Fourier-series expansion of φ. Since the curve

3.8. Let φ be a modular form (cf. 3.6). For g ∈ SL(2, ℤ/n), we denote by gφ the modular form which to a curve with level-n structure (C, α) over S associates the section

(gφ)(C, α) = φ(C, g^{-1}α)

of ω^{⊗k} over S.

The f_{gφ} are the expansions of φ at the cusps. If

u = ±( 1  a ; 0  1 )

and f_φ = ∑ c_m q^m (m ∈ (1/n)ℤ), then

(3.8.1)  f_{uφ} = (−1)^k ∑ c_m ζ_n^{amn} q^m.

Theorem 3.9. Let φ be a modular form of level n and weight k with coefficients in the ℤ[ζ_n]-algebra A.

(i) If the expansions at the cusps f_{gφ} vanish, then φ vanishes.

(ii) If B is a subalgebra of A and the f_{gφ} lie in B[[q^{1/n}]], then φ has coefficients in B (it is obtained by scalar extension from a unique form over B).

Proof. If A is a ℤ[ζ_n]-module, a modular form of level n and weight k with coefficients in A is defined to be an element of

H⁰(𝓜_n, A ⊗_{ℤ[ζ_n]} ω^{⊗k}).

For A an algebra, this definition agrees with 3.6. The Fourier-series expansion f_φ of such a form φ is defined as in 3.7. We have

f_φ ∈ A ⊗_ℤ ℤ[[q^{1/n}]] ⊂ A[[q^{1/n}]].

We shall prove (i) and (ii) under the sole assumption that A and B are modules.
